chapter: Jess Stacy, Goodman and New York characters
title: Refusing to give Goodman's singer an opening
summary: Hodes kept playing the blues when Goodman's girl singer came up, and Goodman left without a word. He says he was thankful to avoid that life.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: again, the only memory I had of him was this. And I was -- Rod Cless was my man and he was in the band. I was with Rod.

So they send this girl up to sing. Now, I don't know I'm being auditioned. Haven't the slightest idea, although Jess told me, he's coming to town. But I figured he's coming in to sit. Or if I'm auditioned, to call me to the table, sit down and talk. None of that. He hears the band play, and the girl goes up to sing with me, and I'm playing the blues. And I won't deviate.

-- give her an opening. And I'm not about to give her an opening because I'm deep in what I'm doing, I'm playing the blues. You want to sing the blues, sing the blues. I'm not stopping you. She just sat at my feet for about five til I got through playing the blues then they minutes, ten minutes, went back to the table. After that, they called for their check and went out.

And that's all I -- I never heard another word. And I thought it was one of the greatest moments, looking back, in my life. I was so thankful, because I avoided that. I didn't need that. That isn't my bag. I want to play and enjoy myself playing. So maybe it kept me from going up the ladder because I didn't go through the ranks. And I thought of that. But there's a price you pay for everything. You want to enjoy what you're doing in music, then you're going to have to forego some of the other things.
